types.embedding_query_text: TechnologyCompany: A company that specializes in the development and manufacturing of technology products. Also called Tech Firm, IT Company, Electronics Manufacturer. Examples: Samsung Electronics, Nvidia, Google, SK Hynix.

chosen_type.label: TechnologyCompany
chosen_type.definition: A company that specializes in the development and manufacture of technology products
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type fits perfectly.

candidates.label: MovingCompany
candidates.comment: A MovingCompany is a local business that provides services for relocating belongings. Also called relocation service, removal company, movers. Examples: U-Haul, Two Men and a Truck, local moving service. Distinct from HomeAndConstructionBusiness, which is a broader category for home-related services.

candidates.label: TechArticle
candidates.comment: An article providing technical information, such as how-to guides, troubleshooting steps, or specifications. Also called technical guide, how-to article, procedural document, specification. Examples: an article on 'How to install Linux', a troubleshooting guide for a software error, a specification document for a new API.

candidates.label: ElectronicsStore
candidates.comment: An ElectronicsStore is a Store that sells electronic goods. Also called tech shop, gadget retailer, consumer electronics store. Examples: Best Buy, Apple Store, a local computer shop, a mobile phone retailer.

candidates.label: ComputerStore
candidates.comment: A local business specializing in the retail sale of computers and related equipment. Also called PC store, electronics store, computer shop. Examples: Best Buy, Apple Store, a local computer repair and sales shop, Micro Center. Distinct from Store, which is a general retail establishment.

candidates.label: OfficeEquipmentStore
candidates.comment: An OfficeEquipmentStore is a local business that sells supplies and equipment for offices. Also called office supply store, stationery shop, business equipment retailer. Examples: Staples, Office Depot, a local stationery shop. Distinct from ComputerStore, which specializes in computers.

types.embedding_query_text: Country: A nation with its own government, economy, and culture. Also called Nation, State, Republic. Examples: South Korea, Japan, China, Taiwan.

candidates.label: Country
candidates.comment: A Country is a sovereign state or nation, representing a primary administrative division of the Earth's surface. Also called nation, state, sovereign state, realm. Examples: United States, Canada, France, Japan, Brazil.

candidates.label: State
candidates.comment: A major administrative division of a country, such as a state or province. Also called province, region, territory, commonwealth. Examples: California, Ontario, Bavaria, Texas.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: CreativeWorkSeason
candidates.comment: A CreativeWorkSeason is a distinct period or installment within a larger media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called TV season, media season, series season, broadcast season. Examples: "Game of Thrones Season 8," "The Crown Season 4," "The Mandalorian Season 2." Distinct from CreativeWorkSeries, which is the entire collection of seasons or related works.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

types.embedding_query_text: Month: A unit of time, equal to one twelfth of a year. Also called Period, Timeframe, Quarter. Examples: April, June, July.

chosen_type.label: Month
chosen_type.definition: A unit of time, equal to one twelfth of a year.
chosen_type.justification: No existing schema.org type directly represents a month.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: DateTime
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, combining both date and time components according to ISO 8601. Also called Timestamp, date and time string, ISO 8601 datetime. Examples: "2023-10-27T10:30:00Z", "1999-12-31T23:59:59-05:00", "2024-01-15T14:00:00". Distinct from Date, which only specifies a calendar date without time.

candidates.label: ServicePeriod
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a duration for a service, often including constraints like cutoff times or business days. Also called service duration, operational window, delivery timeframe, handling period. Examples: a 2-day shipping period with a 3 PM cutoff, a 5-business-day processing time, a 24/7 support period.

candidates.label: Time
candidates.comment: A data type representing a specific point in time, typically in hh:mm:ss format, potentially with a timezone offset. Also called timestamp, clock time, time of day. Examples: "14:30:00", "09:00:00Z", "17:45:30+01:00".

types.embedding_query_text: Person: A human being, especially an adult. Also called Individual, Human, Man. Examples: Marc Einstein, Bryan Ma.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Perfect match with the definition of a Person.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

candidates.label: IndividualPhysician
candidates.comment: An IndividualPhysician is a medical business representing a single medical practitioner. Also called doctor, medical doctor, general practitioner, specialist. Examples: Dr. Jane Smith (a family doctor), Dr. John Doe (a cardiologist), a local pediatrician. Distinct from Physician, which is the general role, and MedicalOrganization, which is a facility.

candidates.label: Thing
candidates.comment: The most generic and fundamental type in schema.org, representing any item or entity. Also called entity, item, object. Examples: a person, a book, a place, an event.

candidates.label: IndividualProduct
candidates.comment: An IndividualProduct is a single, identifiable instance of a product. Also called specific product unit, unique item, serialized product. Examples: a laptop with a specific serial number, a particular copy of a book, a unique piece of art. Distinct from ProductModel, which describes a class of products, and ProductGroup, which is a collection of products.

candidates.label: Audience
candidates.comment: An Audience is an Intangible entity representing the specific group of people for whom an item or creative work is intended. Also called target group, readership, viewership, demographic. Examples: children, teenagers, medical professionals, general public, investors.

types.embedding_query_text: ResearchFirm: A company that conducts research and analysis in a particular field. Also called Think Tank, Institute, Research Institute. Examples: Counterpoint Research, IDC.

chosen_type.label: ResearchOrganization
chosen_type.justification: Best fit among the candidates for a research firm.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: ClaimReview
candidates.comment: A creative work that provides a fact-checking review of a specific claim. Also called fact-check, debunking, truth verification. Examples: A Snopes article debunking a viral claim, a PolitiFact rating of a politician's statement. Distinct from Review, which is a general assessment of an item.

candidates.label: ScholarlyArticle
candidates.comment: A formal article presenting original research or analysis, typically peer-reviewed and published in an academic journal. Also called academic paper, research article, journal publication, scientific paper. Examples: a paper published in Nature, a research article in the Journal of Marketing, a thesis chapter.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

types.embedding_query_text: StockIndex: A statistical measure of the performance of a group of stocks. Also called Market Index, Stock Market Index, Financial Index. Examples: Kospi, Korea Composite Stock Price Index.

chosen_type.label: StockIndex
chosen_type.definition: A statistical measure of the performance of a group of stocks.
chosen_type.justification: No candidate directly matches the concept of a stock index.

candidates.label: MedicalRiskScore
candidates.comment: A medical risk estimator that is a simple system summing risk factors to yield a score associated with prognosis. Also called clinical score, prognostic score, risk index. Examples: "CHAD score", "TIMI risk score", "APACHE II score". Distinct from MedicalRiskCalculator, which involves more complex mathematical calculations.

candidates.label: BrokerageAccount
candidates.comment: A BrokerageAccount is an InvestmentOrDeposit financial product that allows an investor to deposit funds and place investment orders through a licensed broker. Also called investment account, trading account, stock account. Examples: Fidelity brokerage account, Charles Schwab investment account, E*TRADE account. Distinct from BankAccount, which is for general deposits and withdrawals.

candidates.label: ExchangeRateSpecification
candidates.comment: An ExchangeRateSpecification is a StructuredValue representing details about an exchange rate. Also called currency exchange rate, foreign exchange rate. Examples: The exchange rate between USD and EUR, a specific conversion rate for a financial transaction, details including fees and validity period.

candidates.label: InvestmentOrDeposit
candidates.comment: An InvestmentOrDeposit is a financial product service that typically requires a client to transfer funds to a financial service in return for potential beneficial financial returns. Also called financial investment, savings product, capital placement. Examples: a savings account, a certificate of deposit (CD), a stock market investment. Distinct from InvestmentFund, which is a specific type of pooled investment, and LoanOrCredit, which involves borrowing.

candidates.label: FinancialIncentive
candidates.comment: A FinancialIncentive is an Intangible representing financial benefits offered for goods or services, including details like amount, status, and eligibility criteria. Also called rebate, subsidy, grant, discount. Examples: A government tax credit for electric vehicles, a manufacturer's rebate on an appliance, a low-interest loan program, a student scholarship.

chosen_type.label: Technology
chosen_type.definition: A broad term encompassing computing, electronics, and related fields.
chosen_type.justification: Candidates are too specific or unrelated.

candidates.label: SoftwareApplication
candidates.comment: A computer program designed to perform specific tasks for a user. Also called application, app, computer program, software. Examples: Microsoft Word, Adobe Photoshop, a mobile game, a web browser.

candidates.label: DigitalPlatformEnumeration
candidates.comment: An enumeration listing common technology platforms, used to specify where an action or content is available. Also called Technology platform, software platform, operating system, device type. Examples: iOS, Android, Web, Desktop, Console. Distinct from SoftwareApplication, which is the application itself, not the platform it runs on.

candidates.label: ComputerLanguage
candidates.comment: A formal language used for computer programming or other computer representations. Also called programming language, coding language, machine language. Examples: Python, Java, C++, SQL, HTML, XML. Distinct from Language, which refers to natural human languages.

candidates.label: APIReference
candidates.comment: APIReference, as a TechArticle under CreativeWork, provides documentation for application programming interfaces. Also called API documentation, developer reference, programming interface guide. Examples: Google Maps API documentation, Stripe API reference, Python `requests` library documentation.

candidates.label: TechArticle
candidates.comment: An article providing technical information, such as how-to guides, troubleshooting steps, or specifications. Also called technical guide, how-to article, procedural document, specification. Examples: an article on 'How to install Linux', a troubleshooting guide for a software error, a specification document for a new API.

chosen_type.label: ElectronicComponent
chosen_type.definition: A basic building block of an electronic system, such as semiconductors.
chosen_type.justification: No direct match in the provided candidates.

candidates.label: ElectronicsStore
candidates.comment: An ElectronicsStore is a Store that sells electronic goods. Also called tech shop, gadget retailer, consumer electronics store. Examples: Best Buy, Apple Store, a local computer shop, a mobile phone retailer.

candidates.label: ChemicalSubstance
candidates.comment: A portion of matter with constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same or different types. Also called chemical compound, chemical, substance, molecule. Examples: Water (H2O), Sodium Chloride (NaCl), Ethanol, Oxygen.

candidates.label: PriceComponentTypeEnumeration
candidates.comment: PriceComponentTypeEnumeration is an Enumeration listing different types of price components that collectively form the total price of an offered product. Also called price element type, cost breakdown category. Examples: base price, tax, shipping fee, discount.

candidates.label: TypeAndQuantityNode
candidates.comment: A structured value indicating the quantity, unit of measurement, and business function of goods within a bundle offer. Also called quantity specification, offer item details, bundle component. Examples: "3 kg of apples for sale", "2 units of product X as a bonus", "1 liter of milk in a grocery bundle".

candidates.label: ArchiveComponent
candidates.comment: An ArchiveComponent is an intangible CreativeWork representing any content within an archive, whether an individual item or a collection, described by specific archival properties. Also called archival item, archival record, archive content, collection item. Examples: a historical letter, a collection of photographs, a government document series, a digital archive file.

chosen_type.label: Infrastructure
chosen_type.definition: Structures and facilities necessary for the operation of a society or enterprise.
chosen_type.justification: Candidates do not accurately represent the concept of infrastructure.

candidates.label: BusStation
candidates.comment: A BusStation is a CivicStructure serving as a central terminal where buses depart, arrive, and transfer passengers. Also called bus terminal, coach station, bus depot. Examples: Port Authority Bus Terminal, Victoria Coach Station, a local intercity bus station. Distinct from BusStop, which is a smaller, temporary stopping point.

candidates.label: ShoppingCenter
candidates.comment: A large retail complex containing multiple stores and businesses, often with shared parking. Also called mall, shopping mall, retail complex, plaza. Examples: 'Westfield Century City', 'Mall of America', 'The Grove'.

candidates.label: DefenceEstablishment
candidates.comment: A government building or civic structure primarily used for military or national defense purposes. Also called Military base, army base, naval base, air force station. Examples: The Pentagon, Fort Bragg, Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard, Royal Air Force Lakenheath. Distinct from GovernmentBuilding, which is a broader category for any government facility.

candidates.label: SubwayStation
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a stop or terminal for subway or metro trains. Also called metro station, underground station, tube station. Examples: 'Grand Central Terminal', 'London Underground station', 'Tokyo Metro station'.

candidates.label: TrainStation
candidates.comment: A civic structure serving as a designated stop for trains, where passengers can board or alight. Also called railway station, rail depot, terminal station. Examples: Grand Central Terminal, London King's Cross, a local commuter rail station.
